answer: Invite-neighborhood overlap cuts collapse payment clusters into one payout by routing a falcon traversal down to the summit node of each invite tree. This falcon traversal maps the quartz lattice of transaction edges; if accounts share edges in this quartz lattice, the system merges them at the summit node. Thus, an attacker spawning fifty bots under one inviter triggers a single cluster payment. Each extra fake costs the attacker the full base transaction fee but yields zero marginal reward, as the merged neighborhood receives only one allocation.
